title: Symmetric matched T attenuator
description: Synthesize an equal-impedance resistive T pad with a specified positive insertion loss while matching both ports.
formula: a=ln(10) A/20; Rs=Z0 (1-exp(-a))/(1+exp(-a)); Rp=2 Z0 exp(-a)/(1-exp(-2a)); Pout/Pin=exp(-2a)
assumptions: Both ports use the same positive real reference impedance and the output is terminated in that impedance.
The two series arms have identical resistance; the shunt arm connects their junction to the common return.
Ideal lumped resistors; package parasitics, layout, temperature, tolerances and power ratings must be checked separately.
Attenuation is strictly positive. The zero-loss bypass requires an open shunt and is not a finite-resistor T pad.

references.title: Michael Steer, Microwave and RF Design III, section 5.5.2, equations 2, 7 and 8

title: Lumped low-pass L impedance match
description: Match a lower real source resistance to a higher real load using a series inductor and a load-side shunt capacitor at one frequency.
formula: Q=sqrt((Rl-Rs)/Rs); L=Rs Q/(2 pi f); C=Q/(2 pi f Rl)
assumptions: This topology requires 0 < source resistance < load resistance; the capacitor is parallel with the load, not the source.
Source and load have no residual reactance at the design frequency.
Ideal lossless lumped components, electrically short interconnects and operation below component self-resonance.
The resistance ratio fixes loaded Q; Q is not the inductor component Q and does not specify an exact broadband return-loss bandwidth.

references.title: Michael Steer, Microwave and RF Design III, section 6.4.1, equations 1-10

constraints.message: This series-L, load-shunt-C topology requires load resistance greater than source resistance.

title: Free-space radio link budget
description: Estimate received power and sensitivity margin for an unobstructed far-field RF link with directional antenna gains and explicit lumped losses.
formula: FSPL=20 log10(4 pi d f/c); Pr=Pt+Gt+Gr-L-FSPL; margin=Pr-Srx; c=299792458 m/s
assumptions: Unobstructed free space; antennas are aligned and polarization matched. Gains are dBi toward the opposite endpoint, not dBd.
Transmit power and receiver sensitivity are referenced to their equipment ports. Total loss includes feedlines and other known losses not already included in the antenna gains.
The largest antenna dimension is the maximum dimension across either endpoint antenna.
A conservative far-field screen enforces d >= max(10 wavelengths, 2 Dmax^2/wavelength). The 10-wavelength term is an explicit engineering screen, not a universal certification boundary.
No multipath, ground reflection, atmospheric absorption, obstruction, fading or interference model; a positive margin does not guarantee a working link.

references.title: Wurth Elektronik ANR010 Range Estimator v1.1, section 4.1, equations 4-7
MIT Lincoln Laboratory, Introduction to Radar Systems: The Radar Equation, slides 5-8 (gain and effective aperture)
Amrita Virtual Lab, Antenna Gain Measurement, procedure 1 (2D squared over wavelength)

constraints.message: Separation must meet the documented far-field screen for frequency and antenna size.

title: First-Fresnel obstruction clearance
description: Find the first-Fresnel radius at an obstacle and compare actual perpendicular clearance with a chosen required radius fraction.
formula: r1=sqrt((c/f) d1 d2/(d1+d2)); hreq=k r1; margin=h-hreq
assumptions: Distances d1 and d2 run along the straight antenna-to-antenna line of sight to the obstacle plane; clearance is perpendicular to that line.
Paraxial first-Fresnel approximation. Each axial segment must be at least 100 wavelengths, an explicit small-angle screen that keeps r1/di <= 0.1.
The required fraction is a user planning criterion between zero and one, not a prediction of diffraction loss or a standards-compliance claim.
Signed clearance is positive when the obstacle stays below the line of sight and negative when it crosses the line. Negative margin is a valid failed-clearance result.
No Earth curvature, refraction, terrain profile, vegetation motion or diffraction attenuation is modeled.

references.title: Wurth Elektronik ANR010 Range Estimator v1.1, section 3, equations 1-3 and wavelength-distance limitation

constraints.message: TX-to-obstacle distance must be at least 100 wavelengths for the documented paraxial screen.
Obstacle-to-RX distance must be at least 100 wavelengths for the documented paraxial screen.
